partners.diseaseBName: intellectual developmental disorder with polymicrogyria and seizures
partners.mechanism_chain: F-box and Leucine Rich Repeat Protein 3 (HGNC:29710) —DISRUPTS→ Protein folding quality control; TCP1-Chaperonin (HGNC:11607) —DISRUPTS→ Protein folding quality control; Protein folding quality control —DECREASES→ Neuronal development; Neuronal development —LEADS_TO→ intellectual disability, short stature, facial anomalies, and joint dislocations (MONDO:0011651); Neuronal development —LEADS_TO→ intellectual developmental disorder with polymicrogyria and seizures (MONDO:0976124). Loss-of-function mutations in FBXL3 and TCP1 both disrupt protein folding quality control pathways. Impaired protein folding and quality control can lead to downstream defects in neuronal development, manifesting as the distinct but overlapping phenotypes of intellectual disability, short stature, facial anomalies, and joint dislocations (Disease A), and intellectual developmental disorder with polymicrogyria and seizures (Disease B).

falsification.text: The absence of pathogenic variants in TP53 in individuals diagnosed with either intellectual disability, short stature, facial anomalies, and joint dislocations (MONDO:0011651) or hereditary breast carcinoma (MONDO:0016419) would falsify this hypothesis. partners.diseaseBName: hyper-IgE recurrent infection syndrome 1, autosomal dominant
partners.mechanism_chain: FBXL3 (HGNC:27451) —DISRUPTS→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway (WP:WP460); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (WP:WP460) —LEADS_TO→ intellectual disability (HP:0001249); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (WP:WP460) —LEADS_TO→ short stature (HP:0004308); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (WP:WP460) —LEADS_TO→ facial anomalies (HP:0000252); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (WP:WP460) —LEADS_TO→ joint dislocations (HP:0002820); STAT3 (HGNC:11356) —INCREASES→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway (WP:WP460); STAT3 (HGNC:11356) —LEADS_TO→ recurrent infections (HP:0011224). Loss-of-function mutations in FBXL3 disrupt normal cellular processes that may indirectly impact the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, contributing to the phenotypes of intellectual disability, short stature, facial anomalies, and joint dislocations (Disease A). Conversely, gain-of-function mutations in STAT3 directly enhance the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, leading to hyper-IgE syndrome and recurrent infections (Disease B). The convergence occurs at the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, which is dysregulated in both conditions through different mechanisms.
